clue.text: LONDON and PARIS in this case

definitions.text: LONDON and PARIS in this case

parts.words: LONDON and PARIS in this case
parts.note: two capital cities printed in upper-case letters, so they are capitals written in capitals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' is the printer's sense: upper case. The clue prints the city names in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing in all upper-case letters is how forms ask for names, and those cities are national capitals too.

clue.text: Means of communication for landlords

explanation.definitionFit: Written messages sent by post are one way to communicate; landlords are people who let property, so 'let-ters'.

clue.text: Pretentious talk about an insect

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth pompously about an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypocritical, sanctimonious jargon is called cant.

clue.text: Scour lists in civil engineer's contract

indicators.note: the leaning word is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: civil engineer contracted to initials is CE
a ship that lists leans to one side

explanation.surface: A civil engineer's contract is scoured for its lists of terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' is not a legal document here: it tells you to shorten civil engineer to CE. 'Lists' is the verb, as a listing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour something is to scrub it thoroughly clean.

clue.text: Not entirely inclined to favour

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhat biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means incomplete, and also biased towards one side.

clue.text: Excursion in the fall?

explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey, and also a stumble that sends you down.

clue.text: Failed to come up to expectations

definitions.text: Failed to come up to expectations

parts.words: Failed to come up to expectations
parts.note: disappointed people, with 'come up' set against a word for downward

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a plain meaning, but 'come up' teases the opposite direction in the answer's second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappoint someone is to fail them, falling short of what they hoped.

clue.text: Chinese in character, the English have it on a plate

definitions.text: Chinese in character, the English have it on a plate

parts.words: Chinese in character, the English have it on a plate
parts.note: a blue chinoiserie design devised in England and printed on crockery

explanation.walkthrough: This famous blue-and-white design looks Chinese but was created in England in the late 18th century and appears on many English plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-and-white tableware design with a tree, bridge and birds, made in imitation of Chinese porcelain.

clue.text: How gold diggers view their chances?

definitions.text: How gold diggers view their chances?

parts.words: How gold diggers view their chances?
parts.note: prospectors looking ahead to what they might find

explanation.walkthrough: Gold diggers are prospectors, so they see their future in terms of prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospectively means with regard to the future, and prospectors look for ore.

clue.text: Concentrated in a number of Home Counties

parts.note: taken as written
ten is a number
the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: A number of the counties around London are densely populated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense flavours or colours are strong, undiluted.

clue.text: I roll round to have a merry time

indicators.note: the list word wraps round the letter I

parts.note: a roll or roster is a list of names

explanation.surface: Someone rolls about happily to enjoy themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' is not tumbling: it is a list of names, a ROSTER, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel boisterously, celebrating noisily.

clue.text: Sort of life beloved in the old days

indicators.note: sort means to arrange, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A kind of life once held dear.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word meaning dear or gladly, as in 'I would as lief'.

clue.text: Forger's piece coming under the hammer

definitions.text: Forger's piece coming under the hammer

parts.words: Forger's piece coming under the hammer
parts.note: a smith forges metal on a block that is struck by hammers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter and 'under the hammer' an auction; a blacksmith forges iron, and his block is literally under the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron block on which a smith beats hot metal into shape.

clue.text: One's adjustment for long periods

indicators.note: an adjustment changes things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word read with its S as a letter

explanation.surface: Someone's adjustment takes ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immensely long stretches of time.

clue.text: Rage of a theologian rounded by party extremists

indicators.note: the outside letters of the party word surround the rest
the extreme letters of party are its first and last

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A theologian flies into a rage when surrounded by party hardliners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremists' looks like militants but asks for the first and last letters of 'party'; 'rounded by' has those two letters surround the theologian and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a tantrum or fit of temper.

clue.text: Meagre point over 3

indicators.note: in a down answer the point letter sits above the other piece

parts.note: S is south, a compass point
the clue number points to the answer of 3 down, pretentious talk

explanation.surface: A meagre score is a point over three.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' is a cross-reference to the answer at 3 down, not a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, in short supply.

clue.text: We take in a lone man, albeit unprofitable

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: waste that brings no return

indicators.note: the two letters of the first word enclose the others

parts.note: a stag is a man without a female partner, as at a stag party

explanation.surface: We take in a single man, although he brings in nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastage is loss through waste or leakage, the part that yields no profit.

clue.text: Freedom a dog needs

explanation.surface: A dog needs its freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain required a dog licence until 1987.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence is freedom to act; dog owners in Britain once needed a permit for their dog.

clue.text: Dastard in song in pastoral Greece

indicators.note: the villain word is placed inside the song word

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a dastard, a cowardly scoundrel, is a cad

explanation.surface: A villain appears in a song about the Greek countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia, a region of Greece, became the poetic image of rustic paradise.

clue.text: Crook in the clerical profession

parts.note: a bishop's hooked staff, not a criminal priest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a villain; it is the shepherd's staff carried by a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's ceremonial staff, shaped like a shepherd's hook.

clue.text: Hell-flower the teacher once concealed

indicators.note: the letters are kept out of sight inside the phrase

explanation.surface: A teacher once hid a flower from hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword word for a river (it flows). The Acheron is a river of the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Acheron is a river of Hades, the underworld.

clue.text: Taxman caught out creature in detail?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A taxman catches a creature out on a technicality.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'detail' as 'de-tail': a creature without a tail. The Manx cat from the Isle of Man is tailless.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of cat from the Isle of Man born without a tail.

clue.text: As times change, so the artist

indicators.note: change tells us to reorder the letters

explanation.surface: Times change and so does the artist's style.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: Fancy covering an Oriental staple food

parts.note: a cap is a covering for the head or a bottle
rice is a staple food across East Asia

explanation.surface: A lid covers a bowl of Asian rice.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, a sudden impulse.

clue.text: To turn to, it sounds

indicators.note: turning the second word round makes it read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns to listen to a sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It sounds' is not a homophone signal: it is the definition, a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast from a horn, a noise made.

clue.text: Notes a success in the Civil Service

indicators.note: the success word sits inside the service abbreviation

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: Notes about a triumph within government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: Chits are short notes or memos, often vouchers or IOUs.

clue.text: Unscrupulous person with backing of people who matter

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: VIPs, very important people, are those who matter

explanation.surface: A shady character has influential supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPIV is British slang for a flashy small-time crook dealing in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A wartime black-marketeer or petty swindler.

clue.text: Plant slightly socialistic in colour

explanation.surface: A plant with a faintly left-wing tint.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower related to the carnation; mildly left-wing (paler than red); and a pale red hue.

clue.text: Support a surly beast

explanation.surface: Someone props up a bad-tempered animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to hold up; a bear is a large animal, also a gruff person.

clue.text: Amount of precipitation higher in Washington?

definitions.text: Amount of precipitation higher in Washington?

parts.words: Amount of precipitation higher in Washington?
parts.note: both 'wetter' and, read as 'A mount', a peak in that US state

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Amount' as 'A mount': Mount Rainier is a volcano in Washington State. The answer also means wetter.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of rainy, and the name of the highest peak in the Cascades.

clue.text: Copper used for a particular purpose

explanation.surface: A policeman is used for a specific job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is slang for police officer; a 'special' is a part-time volunteer constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A special constable is a volunteer police officer in Britain; special also means designed for one use.

clue.text: Drunk on the dark beer can make one so sad

indicators.note: being drunk mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting drunk on dark beer can make a person maudlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Grief-stricken, especially from a lost love.
